nodes.label: Physical Chemistry
nodes.note: The matter-energy-rates slice of JEE chemistry: gas behaviour, thermodynamics, equilibria, electrochemistry, solutions, solid state, surfaces, kinetics and radioactivity.

nodes.label: Some Basic Concepts of Chemistry
nodes.note: Mole counting, concentration and stoichiometry: the bookkeeping every other physical-chemistry chapter assumes.

nodes.label: Mole Counting and Molar Mass
nodes.note: One mole is a packet of $N_A$ particles; most JEE basics start here.

nodes.label: Concentration Terms
nodes.note: JEE mixes molarity, molality, mole fraction and normality; keep their definitions distinct.

nodes.label: Molarity, Molality, Mole Fraction
nodes.note: $$M = n/V_L,\quad m = n/\text{kg solvent},\quad x_A = n_A/(n_A+n_B)$$. Watch solvent vs solution volume in conversions.

nodes.label: Percentage Composition and Empirical Formula
nodes.note: From mass percentages to the simplest formula, then to the molecular formula from molar mass.

nodes.label: Stoichiometry and Limiting Reagent
nodes.note: Balancing gives mole ratios; the reagent that runs out first caps the product.

nodes.label: Atomic Structure
nodes.note: Models of the atom from Rutherford to the quantum picture; explains line spectra and reactivity trends used across JEE.

nodes.label: Rutherford Nuclear Model
nodes.note: Alpha-scattering showed a tiny dense positive nucleus with most of the atom empty.

nodes.label: Bohr Model and Energy Levels
nodes.note: Quantised circular orbits give hydrogen's spectral lines; a heavy JEE favourite.

nodes.label: Bohr Energy Levels
nodes.note: $$E_n = -13.6/n^2\ \text{eV}$$ for hydrogen; transitions emit $$\Delta E = 13.6\left(1/n_1^2-1/n_2^2\right)\ \text{eV}$$.

nodes.label: Quantum Numbers
nodes.note: n, l, m_l, m_s uniquely label an electron orbital and fix the periodic table's block structure.

nodes.label: Orbitals and Probability Density
nodes.note: Schrodinger picture: orbitals are 3D probability clouds shaped by l; nodes explain bonding.

nodes.label: de Broglie Wavelength
nodes.note: $$\lambda = h/mv = h/p$$. Matter waves set the scale of electron diffraction and orbit stability.

nodes.label: Chemical Bonding
nodes.note: Kept thin for the physical-chemistry graph: only bonding ideas that recur in equilibria, gases and solids.

nodes.label: Lewis Structures, Octet and Hybridisation
nodes.note: Electron bookkeeping predicts geometry and polarity; hybridisation links geometry to sigma/pi bond counts.

nodes.label: VSEPR Geometry
nodes.note: Electron pairs repel to maximise separation; lone pairs compress bond angles.

nodes.label: Bond Order from MO Theory
nodes.note: $$BO = (N_b - N_a)/2$$. Predicts bond strength and $O_2$ paramagnetism; JEE asks $O_2, N_2, O_2^+$.

nodes.label: Redox Reactions
nodes.note: Oxidation numbers and balancing; the bookkeeping that feeds electrochemistry potential calculations.

nodes.label: Oxidation Number Rules
nodes.note: Assign O.N. carefully (peroxide, superoxide, metal hydrides) before classifying agents or balancing.

nodes.label: Oxidation Number Conventions
nodes.note: H = +1 (-1 in metal hydrides), O = -2 (peroxide -1, superoxide -1/2), F = -1, and the O.N. sum equals the species' charge. $$\sum \text{O.N.} = \text{charge on species}$$

nodes.label: Balancing Redox Equations
nodes.note: Half-reaction or oxidation-number change method; conserve atoms, charge and mass.

nodes.label: Disproportionation
nodes.note: One element is both oxidised and reduced in the same reaction, e.g. $Cl_2$ in cold dilute $NaOH$.

nodes.label: Redox Pair -> Galvanic Cell
nodes.note: A spontaneous redox couple sets up a cell: $$\Delta G = -nFE$$, $$E^0_{cell}=E^0_{cathode}-E^0_{anode}$$.

nodes.label: Gaseous State and Kinetic Theory
nodes.note: Ideal-gas laws, gas mixtures and molecular speeds; JEE loves numericals on $v_{rms}$, effusion and van der Waals constants.

nodes.label: Gas Laws (Boyle, Charles, Gay-Lussac)
nodes.note: Each gas law is one variable held constant between two states of a fixed amount of gas.

nodes.label: Boyle's Law
nodes.note: At fixed T, $$PV = const$$. Pressure rises as volume shrinks; basis of lung and piston questions.

nodes.label: Ideal Gas Equation
nodes.note: The combined gas law in one line; underpins almost every gas numerical.

nodes.label: Ideal Gas Equation
nodes.note: $$PV = nRT$$, with $R = 0.0821\ L\ atm\ K^{-1}\ mol^{-1}$. State assumptions: point particles, no intermolecular forces.

nodes.label: Dalton's Law and Graham's Law
nodes.note: Mixture pressures add; rate of effusion scales inversely with sqrt of molar mass.

nodes.label: Dalton's Law of Partial Pressures
nodes.note: $$P_{total} = \sum p_i,\quad p_i = x_i P_{total}$$. Each gas behaves as if alone in the volume.

nodes.label: Graham's Law of Effusion
nodes.note: $$r_1/r_2 = \sqrt{M_2/M_1} = t_2/t_1$$. Diffusion and effusion time problems reduce to square-root-of-mass ratios.

nodes.label: Kinetic Theory Postulates
nodes.note: Gas pressure arises from elastic molecular collisions; average kinetic energy tracks temperature.

nodes.label: Molecular Speeds and Maxwell-Boltzmann
nodes.note: $$v_{rms}=\sqrt{3RT/M},\ v_{avg}=\sqrt{8RT/\pi M},\ v_{mp}=\sqrt{2RT/M}$$. Ratio $v_{rms}:v_{avg}:v_{mp}=\sqrt3:\sqrt{8/\pi}:\sqrt2$.

nodes.label: Degrees of Freedom
nodes.note: Translational, rotational and vibrational modes fix $\gamma = C_p/C_v$ and gas heat capacities.

nodes.label: Real Gases and van der Waals Equation
nodes.note: Finite size (b) and attractions (a) correct the ideal law; $Z$ tracks deviation.

nodes.label: van der Waals Equation
nodes.note: $$\left(P + a n^2/V^2\right)(V - nb) = nRT$$. $a$ measures attraction, $b$ excluded volume; $Z = PV/nRT$.

nodes.label: Critical Constants and Liquefaction
nodes.note: Above $T_c$ no amount of pressure liquefies a gas; critical constants tie back to $a$ and $b$.

nodes.label: Critical Constants from a and b
nodes.note: $$T_c=\frac{8a}{27Rb},\ P_c=\frac{a}{27b^2},\ V_c=3nb$$. Easily the most-asked real-gas formula cluster.

nodes.label: Thermodynamics
nodes.note: State functions, the two laws and Gibbs energy; frames every equilibrium and emf statement in JEE chemistry.

nodes.label: System, Surroundings and State Functions
nodes.note: State functions (U, H, S, G) depend only on endpoints; q and w are path-dependent.

nodes.label: First Law of Thermodynamics
nodes.note: Energy is conserved: heat added and work done by a system change its internal energy.

nodes.label: First Law Equation
nodes.note: $$\Delta U = q + w$$ (chemistry sign convention, w = work done on gas: $w = -P\Delta V$). For isothermal ideal gas, $\Delta U=0$.

nodes.label: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isochoric, Isobaric
nodes.note: Named conditions simplify first-law bookkeeping into one algebraic constraint each.

nodes.label: Entropy and Second Law
nodes.note: Spontaneous processes increase universe entropy; $\Delta S$ of a phase or reaction is computable.

nodes.label: Entropy and Second Law
nodes.note: $$\Delta S_{surr} = -\Delta H_{sys}/T,\quad \Delta S_{univ} > 0$$ for spontaneous. Reversible: $q_{rev}/T$.

nodes.label: Gibbs Free Energy and Spontaneity
nodes.note: $\Delta G$ bundles enthalpy and entropy; negative $\Delta G$ marks a spontaneous process at constant T,P.

nodes.label: Gibbs Free Energy
nodes.note: $$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$$; $\Delta G < 0$ spontaneous, $=0$ equilibrium. Linked to equilibrium: $\Delta G = -RT\ln K$.

nodes.label: Expansion Work
nodes.note: Every numerical on isothermal/adiabatic change starts from the integral form of w.

nodes.label: Work Formulas
nodes.note: Isothermal ideal gas: $$w = -nRT\ln(V_2/V_1)$$; reversible adiabatic: $$w = (P_2V_2-P_1V_1)/(1-\gamma)$$.

nodes.label: Thermochemistry and Energetics
nodes.note: Enthalpy changes with Hess's law, bond enthalpy and calorimetry; classic JEE numerical territory.

nodes.label: Enthalpy and Heat of Reaction
nodes.note: At constant pressure $q_p = \Delta H$; exothermic $\Delta H<0$, endothermic $\Delta H>0$.

nodes.label: Hess's Law and Enthalpy Cycles
nodes.note: Because H is a state function, enthalpy of reaction is path-independent; cycles with heats of formation save time.

nodes.label: Hess's Law
nodes.note: $$\Delta H_{rxn} = \sum \Delta H_{steps}$$. Arrange known formation/combustion data to reach the target reaction.

nodes.label: Bond Enthalpy Calculations
nodes.note: Break bonds (energy in), form bonds (energy out); difference is $\Delta H$.

nodes.label: Bond Enthalpy Formula
nodes.note: $$\Delta H = \sum BE_{\text{broken}} - \sum BE_{\text{formed}}$$. Average bond enthalpies make molecule estimates only.

nodes.label: Calorimetry
nodes.note: Measure q from temperature change with a calorimeter constant; links heat to mass and heat capacity.

nodes.label: Calorimetry Equation
nodes.note: $$q = mc\Delta T + C_{cal}\Delta T$$. Sign and calorimeter constant errors are common traps.

nodes.label: Chemical Equilibrium
nodes.note: How far reactions go and how Le Chatelier shifts them; $K_p$–$K_c$ conversions are exam staples.

nodes.label: Law of Mass Action
nodes.note: Equilibrium constant expression in concentrations of products over reactants, powers = stoichiometric coefficients.

nodes.label: Kp, Kc and Degree of Dissociation
nodes.note: Gas equilibria can use pressures; the two constants differ by $(RT)^{\Delta n}$.

nodes.label: Kp = Kc (RT)^delta n
nodes.note: $$K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n_g}$$. $\Delta n_g$ counts gaseous moles only; $\Delta n_g=0$ makes them equal.

nodes.label: Degree of Dissociation
nodes.note: Fraction dissociated at equilibrium; connects alpha to K and pressure for dimerisation/dissociation.

nodes.label: Degree of Dissociation Relations
nodes.note: For $A \rightleftharpoons 2B$ at pressure P: $$K_p = \frac{4\alpha^2 P}{1-\alpha^2}$$. Solve for $\alpha$ or P.

nodes.label: Le Chatelier's Principle
nodes.note: Changing concentration, pressure or temperature shifts a system to partially undo the change.

nodes.label: Le Chatelier Shift Directions
nodes.note: Add reactant -> forward; increase P shifts toward fewer gas moles; raise T for an endothermic reaction -> forward. Catalyst: equilibrium unchanged. $$K_p = K_c(RT)^{\Delta n}$$ links the gas-phase description.

nodes.label: Ionic Equilibrium, pH and Buffers
nodes.note: Weak electrolytes, pH, buffers, hydrolysis and Ksp; the densest formula cluster in physical chemistry.

nodes.label: Acids and Bases: Arrhenius, Bronsted, Lewis
nodes.note: Each definition is broader than the last; JEE asks for examples fitting each.

nodes.label: Conjugate Acid-Base Pairs
nodes.note: Bronsted: proton donor/acceptor, e.g. $NH_3/NH_4^+$. Lewis: electron-pair acceptor/donor; $BF_3$, $AlCl_3$ are Lewis acids. $$NH_3 + H^+ \rightarrow NH_4^+$$

nodes.label: Water Autoionisation and Kw
nodes.note: Water self-ionises slightly; $K_w$ fixes [H+][OH-] at a given temperature.

nodes.label: Weak Acids/Bases: Ka, Kb
nodes.note: Degree of dissociation of a weak acid grows as it is diluted (Ostwald).

nodes.label: Buffer Solutions
nodes.note: A weak acid/conjugate base pair resists pH change; Henderson–Hasselbalch gives the pH directly.

nodes.label: Henderson-Hasselbalch Equation
nodes.note: $$pH = pK_a + \log\frac{[\text{salt}]}{[\text{acid}]}$$ (acidic buffer). Basic buffer: $pOH = pK_b + \log([\text{salt}]/[\text{base}])$.

nodes.label: Salt Hydrolysis
nodes.note: Salts of weak acid/strong base (or vice versa) hydrolyse, setting solution acidity.

nodes.label: Solubility Product Ksp
nodes.note: Predicts whether a precipitate forms from a mixing; a Q vs Ksp comparison.

nodes.label: Ksp and Molar Solubility
nodes.note: For $M_aX_b$, $$K_{sp} = s^{a+b}a^ab^b$$; e.g. AgCl: $K_{sp}=s^2$, $CaF_2$: $K_{sp}=4s^3$. Common-ion effect lowers s.

nodes.label: Electrochemistry and Ionic Conduction
nodes.note: Conductivity of solutions, Nernst potentials and Faraday's laws; Kohlrausch and Debye-Huckel turn up often.

nodes.label: Conductance and Molar Conductivity
nodes.note: Two ways to report how well a solution conducts; dilution changes them differently.

nodes.label: Molar Conductivity
nodes.note: $$\Lambda_m = \kappa \frac{1000}{c}\ \text{S cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}$$. For strong electrolytes $\Lambda_m$ rises on dilution as inter-ionic drag falls.

nodes.label: Kohlrausch's Law
nodes.note: At infinite dilution each ion contributes independently to conductance; lets you get $K_w$ and $\Lambda^0$ for weak electrolytes.

nodes.label: Debye-Huckel-Onsager Theory
nodes.note: Explains why strong-electrolyte $\Lambda_m$ falls as concentration rises; plots are linear in $\sqrt c$.

nodes.label: Nernst Equation
nodes.note: Electrode potential under non-standard conditions; the link between emf, concentrations and $\Delta G$.

nodes.label: Nernst Equation
nodes.note: $$E = E^0 - \frac{RT}{nF}\ln Q = E^0 - \frac{0.0591}{n}\log Q\ (25^\circ C)$$. Also $\Delta G = -nFE$, $\Delta G^0=-nFE^0$.

nodes.label: Electrolysis and Faraday's Laws
nodes.note: Charge passed deposits a predictable mass; equivalents obey Faraday's constant.

nodes.label: Faraday's Laws
nodes.note: $$m = ZIt/F,\ m \propto Q$$. One faraday ($F = 96487\ C$) deposits one gram-equivalent.

nodes.label: Solutions and Colligative Properties
nodes.note: Raoult and Henry laws, vapour-pressure lowering and the four colligative effects with $i$.

nodes.label: Types of Solutions and Concentration
nodes.note: Solid/liquid/gas mixtures, saturated vs unsaturated, and concentration units used in colligative formulas.

nodes.label: Raoult's Law and Ideal Solutions
nodes.note: Each volatile component contributes partial pressure proportional to its mole fraction.

nodes.label: Raoult's Law
nodes.note: $$P_i = x_i P_i^0,\quad P^0_{mix} = x_A P_A^0 + x_B P_B^0$$. Ideal solutions obey it throughout; positive deviation if $P > \sum x_i P_i^0$.

nodes.label: Relative Lowering of Vapour Pressure
nodes.note: A non-volatile solute lowers the vapour pressure of the solvent; related to solute mole fraction.

nodes.label: Elevation of Boiling Point, Depression of Freezing Point
nodes.note: Dilute solution shifts liquid's boiling/freezing temperatures by amounts proportional to molality.

nodes.label: Delta Tb and Delta Tf
nodes.note: $$\Delta T_b = K_b m,\quad \Delta T_f = K_f m$$. $K_b, K_f$ depend on the solvent; used to find molar masses.

nodes.label: Osmotic Pressure
nodes.note: Pressure needed to stop osmosis through a semipermeable membrane; a colligative property like the others.

nodes.label: Osmotic Pressure Equation
nodes.note: $$\pi = \frac{n}{V}RT = cRT$$. For polymers/proteins where boiling/freezing changes are tiny, $\pi$ is the metric that works.

nodes.label: van't Hoff Factor
nodes.note: Corrects colligative formulas when a solute associates or dissociates in solution.

nodes.label: van't Hoff Factor i
nodes.note: $$i = \frac{\text{observed colligative effect}}{\text{calculated for no association}};\ i = 1+(n-1)\alpha$$. NaCl: $i\approx2$, acetic acid in benzene: $i\approx 1/2$.

nodes.label: Solid State
nodes.note: Crystal lattices, packing efficiencies and defects; density/unit-cell numericals are recurring JEE items.

nodes.label: Crystalline vs Amorphous Solids
nodes.note: Ordered lattice vs short-range order; explains anisotropy, fixed melting points and X-ray diffraction patterns.

nodes.label: Unit Cells and Bravais Lattices
nodes.note: The 14 Bravais lattices tile 3D space; unit-cell geometry (simple, bcc, fcc) fixes coordination and density.

nodes.label: Packing Efficiencies
nodes.note: Simple cubic: 52.4%, bcc: 68%, fcc/ccp: 74%, hcp: 74%. JEE asks for numbers and spheres-per-cell. $$\text{packing efficiency} = \frac{V_{\text{spheres}}}{V_{\text{cell}}}$$

nodes.label: FCC, BCC and HCP Geometry
nodes.note: Atoms touch along body diagonal (bcc) or face diagonal (fcc/hcp); radius relates to edge length.

nodes.label: Density of Unit Cell
nodes.note: Mass of Z atoms in a cube of volume $a^3$ divided by $N_A$ gives crystal density.

nodes.label: Unit Cell Density
nodes.note: $$\rho = \frac{Z M}{a^3 N_A}$$. $Z=1$ (sc), 2 (bcc), 4 (fcc). Watch unit conversions: pm to cm.

nodes.label: Defects in Solids
nodes.note: Point defects create colour and non-stoichiometry; Schottky/Frenkel are the classic pair.

nodes.label: Schottky and Frenkel Defects
nodes.note: Schottky: equal cation/anion vacancies (NaCl); Frenkel: cation shifts to interstitial site (AgBr). Both change density/conductivity. $$\text{Schottky: } n_+ = n_-$$

nodes.label: Surface Chemistry
nodes.note: Adsorption, catalysis and colloids; Freundlich and Langmuir isotherms, plus Tyndall/Brownian behaviour.

nodes.label: Adsorption: Physisorption vs Chemisorption
nodes.note: Surface binding by weak van der Waals or chemical bonds; differ in enthalpy, specificity and reversibility.

nodes.label: Physisorption vs Chemisorption
nodes.note: Physisorption: low $\Delta H$ (20-40 kJ/mol), multilayer, reversible. Chemisorption: higher $\Delta H$ (40-400), monolayer, specific. $$\Delta H_{ads}: \text{phy} < \text{chem}$$

nodes.label: Adsorption Isotherms
nodes.note: Amount adsorbed vs pressure at fixed temperature; Freundlich is empirical, Langmuir assumes a monolayer.

nodes.label: Freundlich Adsorption Isotherm
nodes.note: $$\frac{x}{m} = kP^{1/n}\ (n\ge1)$$. Linear form: $\log(x/m) = \log k + (1/n)\log P$.

nodes.label: Langmuir Isotherm
nodes.note: Monolayer adsorption with equivalent sites: $$\theta = \frac{bP}{1+bP}$$, approaching saturation at high P.

nodes.label: Heterogeneous Catalysis at Surfaces
nodes.note: Reactants adsorb, react and desorb on the solid surface; finely divided metals maximise area. Rate tracks exposed surface area: $r \propto A_{surface}$. $$2H_2 + O_2 \xrightarrow{Pt} 2H_2O$$

nodes.label: Colloids, Tyndall Effect and Emulsions
nodes.note: Dispersed phase in a medium with particle size 1-1000 nm; shows Tyndall scattering and Brownian motion.

nodes.label: Chemical Kinetics
nodes.note: Rate laws, order vs molecularity, half-lives, Arrhenius temperature dependence and catalysis.

nodes.label: Rate of Reaction
nodes.note: Change in concentration per time; average vs instantaneous slopes of concentration-time graphs.

nodes.label: Rate Law, Order and Molecularity
nodes.note: Order is empirical from the rate law; molecularity is theoretical from the rate-determining step.

nodes.label: Rate Law Expression
nodes.note: $$\text{rate} = k[A]^m[B]^n$$; overall order $= m+n$. Order can be fractional/zero; molecularity is 1 or 2.

nodes.label: Zero, First and Second Order
nodes.note: Each order has a characteristic integrated rate law and half-life pattern.

nodes.label: Integrated Rate Laws
nodes.note: Zero: $[A]=[A]_0-kt$. First: $$\ln[A]=\ln[A]_0-kt$$. Second: $1/[A]=1/[A]_0+kt$.

nodes.label: Half-Life of Reactions
nodes.note: Time for half the reactant to react; independence of half-life from concentration flags first order.

nodes.label: Arrhenius Equation
nodes.note: Rate constant rises exponentially with T; higher activation energy means steeper temperature sensitivity.

nodes.label: Arrhenius Equation
nodes.note: $$k = A e^{-E_a/RT}$$. Two-temperature form: $$\ln\frac{k_2}{k_1} = \frac{E_a}{R}\left(\frac{1}{T_1}-\frac{1}{T_2}\right)$$.

nodes.label: Collision Theory
nodes.note: Reaction needs effective collisions: correct orientation and energy above $E_a$.

nodes.label: Nuclear Chemistry and Radioactivity
nodes.note: Decay laws, half-lives and binding energy; pairs with kinetics via exponential decay mathematics.

nodes.label: Alpha, Beta and Gamma Decay
nodes.note: Three emission modes with different penetrating power and mass/atomic number bookkeeping.

nodes.label: Radioactive Decay Law
nodes.note: Undecayed nuclei fall exponentially; a first-order process.

nodes.label: Radioactive Decay Law
nodes.note: $$N = N_0 e^{-\lambda t},\quad A = \lambda N$$. Same math as first-order kinetics.

nodes.label: Half-Life of Radioisotopes
nodes.note: Constant for a given isotope; used in carbon dating and tracer half-thickness.

nodes.label: Radioactive Half-Life
nodes.note: $$t_{1/2} = \frac{\ln 2}{\lambda} = 0.693/\lambda$$. Viel remnant after n half-lives: $(1/2)^n$.

nodes.label: Fission, Fusion and Binding Energy
nodes.note: Mass defect converts to energy; fission of heavy nuclei and fusion of light ones both release binding energy.

nodes.label: Binding Energy and Mass Defect
nodes.note: $$E_b = \Delta m c^2,\quad \Delta m = Z m_p + (A-Z)m_n - M_{nucleus}$$. Per nucleon peaks near Fe-56.
